concept.title: Choose between CIS levels, channels, and generated layers
concept.shortdesc: CIS selection in BPM depends on the intended hardening level and the Firefox schema channel used for validation and export.

section.title: Level 1
section.p: Level 1 is the default starting point for broad enterprise use. In BPM it is represented by generated Level 1 layers for ESR 140.12 and Release 152, each covering 49 mapped recommendations. Use it when the profile should improve security posture while preserving routine browsing and support workflows.

section.title: Level 2
section.p: Level 2 is stricter and adds controls that may affect usability, operations, or troubleshooting. BPM generated Level 2 layers for ESR 140.12 and Release 152, each covering 53 mapped recommendations. Choose it only when the deployment owner accepts stronger restrictions and has a review process for exceptions.

section.title: Supported Firefox channels
section.p: BPM currently validates CIS layers against Firefox ESR 140.12 and Firefox Release 152 schemas. A recommendation topic may link to a Firefox policy or managed preference that is valid in both channels, but you still need to keep the selected schema channel consistent until export.

section.title: Generated layers
section.p: The available generated layers are cis-l1.esr-140.12, cis-l1.release-152, cis-l2.esr-140.12, and cis-l2.release-152. Each layer contributes BPM-owned policy values or locked managed preferences, then the profile merge logic records whether a value was added, already satisfied, replaced, stricter in the base, or kept for manual review.

section.title: Manual review
section.p: Nine explicit paths require manual review because local governance can change the correct decision. Update controls, proxy mode and lock state, and selected sanitize-on-shutdown values are examples where BPM surfaces the issue but does not make a universal compliance decision.
